services.title: Homeowners Insurance
services.summary: The six standard coverages on a Texas home.
services.text: A standard Texas homeowners policy carries six coverages, protecting the structure, what is inside it and your liability for what happens on the property.
services.lead: A standard homeowners insurance policy in Texas typically provides six main types of coverage to protect your home, belongings and financial assets from common risks like fire, theft and windstorms.
services.imageAlt: A white house with a wrap-around porch under a blue sky

covers.title: Dwelling (Coverage A)
covers.text: Pays to repair or rebuild the physical structure of your home — roof, walls, foundation — and attached structures like a garage.

covers.title: Other Structures (Coverage B)
covers.text: Covers detached structures on your property, including fences, sheds and detached garages.

covers.title: Personal Property (Coverage C)
covers.text: Protects your belongings, such as furniture, clothing and electronics, even if they are damaged or stolen while you are away from home.

covers.title: Loss of Use (Coverage D)
covers.text: Pays for temporary housing, food and other essential costs if a covered disaster makes your home uninhabitable during repairs.

covers.title: Personal Liability (Coverage E)
covers.text: Provides legal defense and payment if you are held responsible for accidentally injuring someone else or damaging their property.

covers.title: Medical Payments (Coverage F)
covers.text: Pays medical bills for people other than household members who are accidentally hurt on your property.

questions.q: Does a homeowners policy cover flood damage?
questions.a: No. Flood is a separate policy in Texas, and we usually quote the two together.

questions.q: Is wind and hail included?
questions.a: In most of Texas it is part of the homeowners policy, but along the coast it is often excluded and has to be bought separately.

services.title: Condo and Townhouse Insurance (HO-6)
services.summary: Walls-in coverage for a condo or townhome.
services.text: An HO-6 policy covers the walls-in portion of your unit, your belongings and your liability, filling the gaps the HOA master policy leaves.
services.lead: Owning a condo or townhome comes with its own responsibilities. While your Homeowners Association master policy generally protects the building's exterior and common areas, your personal HO-6 policy fills the gaps for everything inside your unit.

covers.title: Building property (walls-in)
covers.text: Protects the interior structure of your unit, including drywall, flooring, cabinetry, countertops and built-in appliances.

covers.title: Personal property
covers.text: Covers belongings such as furniture, electronics, clothing and kitchenware against fire, theft or vandalism.

covers.title: Personal liability
covers.text: Financial protection if a guest is injured inside your condo, or if you accidentally damage a neighbor's property — a leak from your unit, for example.

covers.title: Additional living expenses
covers.text: Pays for hotel stays, meals and other costs if a covered event makes your condo uninhabitable during repairs.

covers.title: Loss assessment
covers.text: Helps cover your portion of special assessments charged by the HOA when communal damage exceeds the master policy's limits.

covers.title: What the HOA master policy leaves you
covers.text: How much you need depends on the master policy type. Bare walls means you insure everything inside, including the fixtures. Single entity covers the original fixtures, so you insure your upgrades and belongings. All-in covers most structural items and improvements, leaving personal property as your main concern.

questions.q: What weather does an HO-6 policy cover in Texas?
questions.a: Policies typically cover damage from fire, windstorms, hail and lightning.

questions.q: Is flooding included?
questions.a: No. Standard condo policies in Texas do not cover flood damage, so it has to be written separately, and that matters most in a high-risk area like the Gulf Coast.

questions.q: Is there a separate deductible for wind and hail?
questions.a: Many Texas policies carry a separate deductible for wind and hail damage, often a percentage rather than a flat figure, because of how often severe storms hit the state.

questions.q: What add-ons are worth looking at?
questions.a: Water backup, which covers sewage and drain backups that base policies usually exclude; replacement cost coverage, so you are paid what a new item costs rather than a depreciated value; and valuable items floaters for jewelry, art or specialized equipment above the standard limits.

services.title: Renters Insurance
services.summary: Belongings, liability and loss of use.
services.text: Renters insurance covers personal property, liability and additional living expenses if a rental becomes uninhabitable. The state does not require it, but many landlords do.
services.lead: Renters insurance in Texas covers your personal property, your liability and your additional living expenses if a rental becomes uninhabitable. It is not required by state law, but many landlords mandate it. Policies typically cover theft, fire, smoke, vandalism and water damage, though flood insurance is usually separate.

covers.title: Personal property protection
covers.text: Replaces belongings — a laptop, clothes — if they are stolen or damaged, even outside the home.

covers.title: Liability coverage
covers.text: Protects you if you accidentally cause damage to the property or to someone else's property.

covers.title: Medical payments
covers.text: Covers medical bills if a guest is injured at your place.

covers.title: Additional living expenses
covers.text: Covers hotel, rent or food costs if you have to move out temporarily after a covered loss such as a fire.

questions.q: Does my landlord's insurance cover my things?
questions.a: No. Landlord insurance does not cover your personal belongings.

questions.q: Should I choose replacement cost or actual cash value?
questions.a: Opt for replacement cost value over actual cash value, so you get the cost of buying new items rather than their depreciated value. Document what you own with photos or video to speed up a claim.

questions.q: Are my roommates covered?
questions.a: Some policies cover roommates and some do not, so check before you assume they are included.

questions.q: Are there discounts on a renters policy?
questions.a: You may get one for a security system or fire alarms, or for bundling the policy with your auto insurance.

services.title: Windstorm Insurance
services.summary: Wind and hail along the Texas coast.
services.text: In 14 coastal counties and parts of Harris County, wind and hail are often excluded from the homeowners policy and have to be bought separately, frequently through TWIA.
services.lead: Texas windstorm insurance covers property damage caused by wind and hail. In most of Texas that coverage sits inside a standard homeowners policy, but in 14 coastal counties and parts of Harris County it is often excluded and must be purchased separately.
services.imageAlt: A storm shelf cloud moving in over the ocean

covers.title: The Texas Windstorm Insurance Association
covers.text: TWIA is the state's insurer of last resort, providing wind and hail coverage for coastal property owners who cannot get it from private companies. TWIA policies cover wind and hail only — not fire, theft or flood.

covers.title: Who qualifies
covers.text: You must have been denied coverage by at least one private insurer, be located in one of the 14 designated coastal counties or eastern Harris County, and hold a Windstorm Certificate of Compliance (WPI-8 or WPI-8E).

covers.title: First-tier counties
covers.text: Aransas, Brazoria, Calhoun, Cameron, Chambers, Galveston, Jefferson, Kenedy, Kleberg, Matagorda, Nueces, Refugio, San Patricio and Willacy, plus the portion of Harris County east of Highway 146.

covers.title: What it costs
covers.text: Property value, location and the deductible you choose all affect the rate.

questions.q: Can I buy a TWIA policy directly?
questions.a: No. You have to apply through a Texas-licensed insurance agent.

questions.q: Can I get a policy once a hurricane is coming?
questions.a: No. You cannot purchase or change a TWIA policy once a hurricane has entered the Gulf of Mexico.

questions.q: Does windstorm cover flooding?
questions.a: No. Neither a standard homeowners policy nor a TWIA policy typically covers flood damage. That needs a separate policy, usually through the National Flood Insurance Program.

services.title: Flood Insurance
services.text: Flood is always a separate policy, because standard homeowners and renters insurance does not cover damage from rising water.
services.lead: In Texas, flood insurance is a separate policy because standard homeowners and renters insurance typically does not cover damage from rising water. It is not required by state law, but it is often mandatory for homeowners with federally backed mortgages in high-risk zones.
services.imageAlt: A flooded residential street with water up around a house

covers.title: National Flood Insurance Program
covers.text: Managed by FEMA. NFIP policies offer up to $250,000 for the building and $100,000 for contents, and generally carry a 30-day waiting period.

covers.title: Private flood insurance
covers.text: Often provides higher limits — up to around $7 million — shorter waiting periods of around 10 to 14 days, and extras such as loss of use coverage for temporary living expenses.

covers.title: The TWIA requirement
covers.text: If you carry TWIA coverage and your home was built or altered after September 1, 2009 in a high-risk zone, you must also have flood insurance.

covers.title: Renters
covers.text: Texas law (HB 531) requires landlords to disclose whether a property sits in a 100-year floodplain or has flooded in the past five years. Renters are encouraged to buy contents-only policies.

questions.q: How long before a flood policy takes effect?
questions.a: Most policies have a 10- to 30-day waiting period before they become active, so do not wait until a storm is in the forecast.

questions.q: How do I find out my flood risk?
questions.a: You can look up your property's specific risk using the FEMA Flood Map Service Center.

services.title: Auto Insurance
services.text: Texas requires liability coverage of 30/60/25. We write that and the coverage that goes around it — collision, comprehensive, PIP and uninsured motorist.
services.lead: Auto insurance in Texas is a mandatory contract that provides financial protection against car-related losses. Texas is an at-fault state, meaning the responsible driver's insurance covers accident costs. The legal minimum, known as 30/60/25, covers $30,000 for injuries per person, $60,000 for total injuries per accident and $25,000 for property damage.
services.imageAlt: Elevated highway overpasses on the Texas Gulf Coast

covers.title: Liability coverage
covers.text: Required. Pays for damages and injuries you cause to others, at the 30/60/25 minimum or above.

covers.title: Collision coverage
covers.text: Pays for repairs to your car regardless of who caused the accident.

covers.title: Comprehensive coverage
covers.text: Covers damage from non-collision events such as theft, fire, hail or vandalism.

covers.title: Personal injury protection
covers.text: Covers medical bills, lost wages and caregiver costs for you and your passengers, regardless of fault.

covers.title: Uninsured and underinsured motorist
covers.text: Pays for injuries or damage when the other driver has no insurance or not enough of it.

questions.q: Do I have to take uninsured motorist coverage?
questions.a: It is not legally required, but insurers must offer it and you have to reject it in writing if you do not want it.

questions.q: What does my lender require?
questions.a: If you are leasing or financing a car, lenders usually require both collision and comprehensive coverage.

questions.q: Do I need to carry proof of insurance?
questions.a: Yes. You must be able to show proof of insurance when law enforcement asks for it.

services.title: Boat and PWC Insurance
services.text: Texas does not require boat or personal watercraft insurance, but lenders, marinas and some public waterways do.
services.lead: In Texas, boat and personal watercraft insurance is not required by state law. It is still worth having, and third parties often insist on it: lenders usually require full coverage on a financed boat or Jet Ski, many marinas and private docks require proof of liability before you can dock or store a vessel, and some public lakes and organized events mandate it.
services.imageAlt: Boats docked at a pier on the water at sunset

covers.title: Liability coverage
covers.text: Protects you if you cause bodily injury or property damage to others.

covers.title: Hull and physical damage
covers.text: Covers repairs or replacement of your vessel after an accident, fire, theft or storm.

covers.title: Medical payments
covers.text: Pays medical bills for you or your passengers if someone is injured in an accident.

covers.title: Towing and roadside assistance
covers.text: Help if your boat breaks down on the water, or if the trailer has trouble on the road.

covers.title: Uninsured and underinsured boater
covers.text: Covers your injuries if you are hit by a boater who does not have adequate insurance.

questions.q: What does a PWC policy cost?
questions.a: Liability-only policies for Jet Skis can start around $100 to $150 a year, while full coverage typically runs $200 to $600 depending on the craft's performance and value.

questions.q: What does boat insurance cost in Texas?
questions.a: The average annual cost in Texas was about $640 in 2024, though simple liability-only policies can be found for as low as $100 a year. A rule of thumb is roughly 1.5 percent of the boat's value.

services.title: Motorcycle Insurance
services.text: Texas requires riders to carry the same minimum liability limits as drivers, with collision, comprehensive and custom parts coverage available on top.
services.lead: Texas requires motorcycle riders to carry minimum liability insurance, often called the 30/60/25 rule: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident and $25,000 for property damage. Uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage must also be offered to you.

covers.title: Minimum liability
covers.text: $30,000 per person, $60,000 per accident and $25,000 for property damage, which is what proves financial responsibility.

covers.title: Collision
covers.text: Covers damage to your bike from an accident.

covers.title: Comprehensive
covers.text: Covers non-collision damage such as theft, fire and vandalism.

covers.title: Custom parts and equipment
covers.text: Protects specialized add-ons that a standard policy would not cover.

covers.title: Mopeds and scooters
covers.text: Motor-driven cycles with smaller engines need the same liability coverage as motorcycles.

questions.q: What affects the premium?
questions.a: Age, driving record, riding experience, location and the type of bike. Many insurers also discount for completing a safety course, bundling policies or belonging to a riders' association.

questions.q: What happens if I ride uninsured?
questions.a: Riding without insurance in Texas is illegal and carries penalties similar to driving a car uninsured. You have to carry proof of insurance while riding, and failing to produce it can mean fines, license suspension or impoundment.

questions.q: Do I have to take uninsured motorist and PIP?
questions.a: Texas law requires insurers to offer, and in some cases include, uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage and personal injury protection, so you have to reject them in writing if you do not want them.

services.title: RV and Travel Trailer Insurance
services.summary: Motorhomes, fifth wheels and travel trailers.
services.text: What Texas requires depends on whether the RV is motorized or towable. Motorhomes need 30/60/25 liability; towable trailers do not need their own policy, but your tow vehicle will not cover damage to them.
services.lead: In Texas, RV insurance requirements depend strictly on whether your vehicle is motorized or towable. Self-propelled motorhomes must meet the same minimum liability standards as cars, while towable trailers like fifth wheels generally do not require a separate state-mandated policy.

covers.title: Motorhomes (Class A, B or C)
covers.text: Legally required to carry 30/60/25 liability to operate on public roads. Texas law also requires insurers to offer at least $2,500 in personal injury protection, and many RV policies offer more. A financed motorhome usually needs collision and comprehensive too.

covers.title: Towable RVs
covers.text: Not legally required to carry separate insurance in Texas. Your tow vehicle's liability often extends to the trailer while it is attached, but that does not cover damage to the trailer itself or its contents.

covers.title: Comprehensive coverage
covers.text: Strongly worth having in Texas because of hail risk. Covers non-collision events like fire, theft and storm damage.

covers.title: Vacation liability
covers.text: Covers accidents that happen at your campsite while the RV is parked and being used as a residence.

covers.title: Full-timer's coverage
covers.text: For people who live in the RV year-round, combining personal liability and property protection much like a homeowners policy.

covers.title: Personal effects coverage
covers.text: Protects the belongings inside the RV, such as gear and electronics.

questions.q: My travel trailer is not required to be insured. Should I insure it anyway?
questions.a: Your tow vehicle's liability covers what the trailer does to others while attached, but nothing that happens to the trailer or what is inside it. A separate policy is what covers that.

services.title: ATV Insurance
services.summary: Off-road coverage that a home policy will not carry.
services.text: Texas does not require ATV insurance on private property, but public riding areas, lenders and the limits of your homeowners policy all push toward a dedicated policy.
services.lead: In Texas, ATV insurance is not legally required by state law for operation on private property. Liability insurance is often mandatory, though, if you plan to ride in state parks, national forests or other designated public riding areas.

covers.title: Liability coverage
covers.text: Covers bodily injury and property damage you cause to others. Recommended limits are often higher than standard auto policies because of the injury risk.

covers.title: Collision coverage
covers.text: Pays for repairs to your ATV after an accident, regardless of who is at fault.

covers.title: Comprehensive coverage
covers.text: Protects against theft, fire, vandalism, and damage from natural disasters or animals.

covers.title: Uninsured and underinsured motorist
covers.text: Protects you if you are hit by another rider who does not have adequate insurance.

covers.title: Medical payments
covers.text: Covers medical expenses for you and your passengers after an accident.

questions.q: Does my homeowners policy cover my ATV?
questions.a: Most standard homeowners policies offer very limited coverage, or none at all, once the ATV leaves your private property.

questions.q: Do I still need a title in Texas?
questions.a: Yes. Texas no longer requires ATV registration at county tax offices, but you are still required to have a title for the vehicle.

questions.q: Does a lender require coverage?
questions.a: If the ATV is financed or leased, lenders typically require you to carry collision and comprehensive coverage for as long as the loan runs.

services.title: Golf Cart Insurance
services.summary: Required once you drive on public streets.
services.text: Whether you need coverage depends on where you drive. On public streets under a local ordinance, the state's minimum liability limits apply.
services.lead: In Texas, golf cart insurance requirements depend primarily on where you drive. There is no statewide mandate for insurance on private property, but coverage is generally required by law if you operate your cart on public roads under a local ordinance, typically streets with speed limits of 35 mph or less.

covers.title: Minimum liability on public streets
covers.text: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury per accident and $25,000 for property damage.

covers.title: Low-speed vehicles
covers.text: If your vehicle is registered as a Low-Speed Vehicle rather than a standard golf cart, insurance is strictly mandatory and you must carry proof of it along with your driver's license.

covers.title: Collision
covers.text: Repairs your cart after an accident, regardless of fault.

covers.title: Comprehensive
covers.text: Protects against theft, vandalism and Texas weather such as hail and hurricanes.

covers.title: Medical payments and uninsured motorist
covers.text: Helps with medical bills for you and your passengers, and protects you if you are hit by someone without insurance.

questions.q: Will my home or auto policy cover the cart?
questions.a: Most standard home or auto policies offer very limited protection once the cart leaves your property.

services.title: Umbrella Insurance
services.summary: Liability that starts where your other limits stop.
services.text: Umbrella insurance picks up after your auto or homeowners liability limits are exhausted, usually starting at $1 million.
services.lead: Umbrella insurance in Texas acts as an extra layer of liability protection that kicks in after your primary auto or homeowners limits are exhausted. It is not required by state law, but it is worth looking at for Texans with significant assets, high income potential or specific risks such as pools and teenage drivers.

covers.title: Excess liability
covers.text: Pays for medical bills, property damage and legal settlements when costs exceed your standard policy limits, often starting at $1 million.

covers.title: Legal defense
covers.text: Covers attorney fees and court costs, even if a lawsuit is groundless.

covers.title: Expanded protection
covers.text: Covers incidents typically excluded by standard policies, such as libel, slander, false arrest and invasion of privacy.

covers.title: Worldwide coverage
covers.text: Most policies protect you for incidents that occur anywhere in the world, not just in Texas.

questions.q: What does it cost?
questions.a: Estimated annual premiums in Texas run between $150 and $400 for the first $1 million in coverage. Each additional $1 million increment typically costs between $50 and $100 more per year.

questions.q: Who should consider it?
questions.a: People who own a home or rental property, have risky amenities such as a swimming pool, a trampoline or certain dog breeds, have teenage drivers on the policy, drive a great deal, or want to protect future earnings from being garnished after a judgment that exceeds their policy limits.

questions.q: Do my other policies need higher limits first?
questions.a: Usually, yes. Most Texas insurers require you to carry high liability limits on the underlying policies — $250,000 and $500,000 on auto, for example — before they will issue an umbrella policy over the top.

questions.q: What does an umbrella policy not cover?
questions.a: Your own injuries, damage to your own property, intentional criminal acts, and business-related liabilities, which need a commercial umbrella policy instead.

about.title: A family-operated independent agency.
text: Alber Insurance Agency is a family-operated business with deep roots in its local community, and those family values drive every interaction we have with our clients.

Insurance can be complex, which is why we take the time to listen to what you need and tailor the coverage to protect what matters most to you. Because we represent multiple insurance carriers rather than one company, we can compare policies and place you with the one that fits.
The office is open Monday to Thursday from 9 AM to 4 PM and Friday morning, or by appointment.

faqs.q: What does an independent agency do differently?
faqs.a: Unlike captive agents who represent a single insurance company, independent agents work with multiple insurers. That lets us compare policies and prices and find the option that fits you.

faqs.q: Does my homeowners policy cover flooding?
faqs.a: No. Standard homeowners and renters insurance in Texas does not cover damage from rising water. Flood is always a separate policy.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate windstorm policy?
faqs.a: In most of Texas wind and hail sit inside the homeowners policy. In the 14 coastal counties and parts of Harris County they are often excluded and have to be purchased separately, frequently through TWIA.

faqs.q: How long before a flood policy takes effect?
faqs.a: NFIP policies generally have a 30-day waiting period, and private flood policies often 10 to 14 days. Do not wait for a storm to be in the forecast.

faqs.q: What are the minimum auto liability limits in Texas?
faqs.a: 30/60/25 — $30,000 for injuries per person, $60,000 for total injuries per accident, and $25,000 for property damage.

faqs.q: Can I come in outside office hours?
faqs.a: Yes. The office is open Monday to Thursday from 9 AM to 4 PM and Friday morning, and we also see clients by appointment.
